body: [News • 5 days ago Warsh speaks](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/kevin-warsh-fed-will-not-be-comfortable-with-inflation-above-2-183000837.html?.tsrc=fin-notif). [Stocks fell on Wednesday](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-losses-accelerate-after-fed-decision-as-powell-touts-inflation-worries-185152647.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead)and [Thursday](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-recover-from-steep-losses-as-oils-surge-eases-200040220.html) after Fed Chair Jerome Powell underscored the uncertainty surrounding the oil shock during his press conference and said the US had not made as much progress on inflation as it had hoped. > In comments to reporters on Wednesday, Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell acknowledged that the oil crisis resulting from the Iran war [could drive up inflation](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/federal-reserve-holds-interest-rates-steady-keeps-1-cut-in-play-this-year-as-uncertainty-mounts-130010108.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead). > Even as he said “there will be some effects on inflation going forward," the Fed chair stuck to the same line when asked to make predictions about just how large the effects of the war in the Middle East could be: "The implications of [developments in the Middle East](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-futures-fall-oil-surges-after-iran-inflation-worries-sink-stocks-225027246.html?pl2=everyday-hero_lead) on the US economy are uncertain.". Aimee Picchi is the associate managing editor for CBS MoneyWatch, where she covers business and personal finance. The Federal Reserve on Wednesday left its benchmark interest rate unchanged amid resurgent inflation, but nearly half of its policymakers said they would support a rate hike later this year. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept the federal funds rate, which affects borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, in its current range of 3.5% to 3.75%**.**Economists had widely expected the central bank to keep rates steady. "You might have already noticed something, a difference in today's policy statement," Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said in a press conference to discuss the Fed's latest interest rate decision. The Fed also released its Summary of Economic Projections(SEP) on Wednesday, which shows that nearly half of FOMC members said they could support a rate hike later this year. Warsh noted that the FOMC's economic projections show the federal funds rate will sit at 3.8% at the end of 2026 and 3.6% at the end of 2027.
